You're helping build a thorough understanding of a repo for its front-end dev lead. This is "Zimmermann" — a client website-redesign/handover project built on the "Agentic Design Workflow" (ADW) template: a structured, skill-driven way of working for design and delivery teams, covering discovery, design documentation, prototyping, and requirements.

Repo root: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/Zimmermann-Handover

Your scope is ONLY `.claude/skills/`. This folder contains the actual workflow engine: each subfolder is a slash-command skill triggered by a team member. Read EVERY `SKILL.md` in full (not excerpts) under these folders: `_shared`, `add-to-viewer`, `capture-feedback`, `deploy-catalog`, `deploy-viewer`, `extract`, `handover`, `initiate-design-project`, `requirements-scan`, `setup`, `setup-ai`, `setup-local`, `start-prototype`, `update-context`, `workshop`. Also read whatever reference files live under `_shared/` (e.g. there should be `atomic-model.md` and `authoring.md` — portable rule files read explicitly by `/extract`, `/deploy-catalog`, and `/handover`, NOT summarized into project-context.md). If any skill folder contains additional reference docs beyond SKILL.md (e.g. `extract/library.md`, `handover/index-generator.md` — check what's actually there), read those too since some skills are known to split detailed steps into companion files.

Background you can assume: the repo's top-level structure is `01-context/` (knowledge base), `02-design/` (library/catalog/specs/prototypes/viewer), `03-requirements/` (epics/features/stories), `04-feedback/` (Figma comment exports), `05-handover/` (engineering handover ToC), `06-tools/` (vendored MCP tools). You don't need to re-verify folder contents — focus entirely on what the skills say they do.

Report back (this feeds into a larger consolidated report — use clear headers, be thorough but organized, no fluff):
- **Per-skill summary**: for each of the 14 skills (excluding `_shared`), 1-3 sentences: what triggers it, what it reads as input, what it writes/modifies. Group them roughly by lifecycle stage (setup → context building → design/extraction → prototyping → requirements → handover → deployment) rather than alphabetically.
- **`_shared` rules**: what `atomic-model.md` and `authoring.md` (and anything else in `_shared/`) actually specify, and which skills consume them.
- **Interconnections**: a short map of which skills' outputs feed which other skills' inputs (e.g. `/extract` writes the contract that `/deploy-catalog` and `/handover` both read from).
- **`/extract` detail**: this is the most complex skill — per project decision history, it has four modes (full library extraction, library-wide re-extraction/diff, single-component re-extraction, regenerate-from-contract). Confirm this against the actual SKILL.md and describe each mode briefly.
- **Anomalies**: anything a skill references (a file, folder, or another skill) that doesn't actually exist elsewhere in the repo, or instructions that look internally inconsistent.

This is a read-only research task — do not modify any files. Keep the final report focused and skimmable.

Trigger whenever the user wants a new blank Figma file — a new design, FigJam, or Slides file — or when you need a fresh file before calling `use_figma`. Usage — /figma-create-new-file [editorType] [fileName] (e.g. /figma-create-new-file figjam My Whiteboard, /figma-create-new-file slides Q3 Review)
- figma:figma-design-to-code: Use this skill when implementing a Figma design as code (design → code) — the read-FROM-Figma direction. Triggers: 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'code this up from Figma', 'design to code', or a figma.com design URL provided alongside a codebase. Encodes the workflow for reading a node out of Figma with get_design_context and adapting its reference output to the target project — reusing existing components, tokens, and conventions, and honoring Code Connect mappings, component docs, design annotations, and design tokens by priority. Complements figma-code-connect (component mapping) and figma-generate-design / figma-use (the reverse, code → design direction).
- figma:figma-generate-design: Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code', 'convert this modal/dialog/drawer/panel to Figma'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, or any composed multi-section view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles from Code Connect files, existing screens, and library search, then imports them and assembles views incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.
- figma:figma-generate-diagram: MANDATORY prerequisite — load this skill BEFORE every `generate_diagram` tool call. NEVER call `generate_diagram` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user asks to create, generate, draw, render, sketch, or build a diagram — flowchart, architecture diagram, sequence diagram, ERD or entity-relationship diagram, state diagram or state machine, gantt chart, or timeline. Also trigger when the user mentions Mermaid syntax or wants a system architecture, decision tree, dependency graph, API call flow, auth handshake, schema, or pipeline visualized in FigJam. Routes to type-specific guidance, sets universal Mermaid constraints, and tells you when to use a different diagram type or skip the tool entirely (mindmaps, pie charts, class diagrams, etc.).
- figma:figma-generate-library: Build or update a professional-grade design system in Figma from a codebase. Use when the user wants to create variables/tokens, build component libraries, create individual components with proper variant sets and variable bindings, set up theming (light/dark modes), document foundations, or reconcile gaps between code and Figma. Also use when the user asks to create or generate any component in Figma — even a single one — since components require proper variable foundations, variant states, and design token bindings to be production-quality. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.
- figma:figma-implement-motion: Translates Figma motion and animations into production-ready application code. Use when implementing animation/motion from a Figma design — user mentions "implement this motion", "add animation from Figma", "animate this component", provides a Figma URL whose node is animated, or when `get_design_context` returns motion data or instructs you to call `get_motion_context`.
- figma:figma-swiftui: SwiftUI ↔ Figma translation. Triggers on phrases like 'implement this Figma design in SwiftUI', 'build this screen in Swift', 'push this SwiftUI view to Figma', 'mirror my Swift code in a Figma file', or whenever a Figma URL appears alongside `.swift` files / an `.xcodeproj`. Skipping it causes common, hard-to-debug failures. Use this skill when the user mentions microfrontends, multi-zones, splitting an app across teams, independent deployments, cross-app routing, incremental migration, composing multiple frontends under one domain, microfrontends.json, @vercel/microfrontends, the microfrontends local proxy, or path-based routing between Vercel projects. - vercel:turbopack: Turbopack expert guidance. Use when configuring the Next.js bundler, optimizing HMR, debugging build issues, or understanding the Turbopack vs Webpack differences.

Use when configuring platform-level security, responding to attacks, or staging firewall rules.
- vercel:vercel-functions: Vercel Functions expert guidance — Serverless Functions, Edge Functions, Fluid Compute, streaming, Cron Jobs, and runtime configuration. Use when configuring, debugging, or optimizing server-side code running on Vercel.
- vercel:vercel-sandbox: Vercel Sandbox guidance — ephemeral Firecracker microVMs for running untrusted code safely. Supports AI agents, code generation, and experimentation. Use when executing user-generated or AI-generated code in isolation.
- vercel:vercel-storage: Vercel storage expert guidance — Blob, Edge Config, and Marketplace storage (Neon Postgres, Upstash Redis). Use when choosing, configuring, or using data storage with Vercel applications.
- vercel:verification: Full-story verification — infers what the user is building, then verifies the complete flow end-to-end: browser → API → data → response. Triggers on dev server start and 'why isn't this working' signals.
- vercel:workflow: Vercel Workflow DevKit (WDK) expert guidance. Use when building durable workflows, long-running tasks, API routes or agents that need pause/resume, retries, step-based execution, or crash-safe orchestration with Vercel Workflow.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	# Atomic model: how we classify components
2	
3	The single rule that decides whether a UI element is an **atom**, **molecule**,
4	**organism**, **template**, or **page**. It is transitive and machine-checkable (see
5	`02-design/library/contract/validate.mjs`). The contract records the tier for
6	every component at the atom, molecule, and organism level only.
7	
8	---
9	
10	## The five tiers
11	
12	| Tier | Definition (by what the component's **own template renders**) |
13	|---|---|
14	| **Atom** | Renders **no other component**: markup + CSS + tokens only. |
15	| **Molecule** | Renders **only atoms**. |
16	| **Organism** | Renders **at least one molecule**. |
17	| **Template** | Defines the **skeletal page frame**: a set of named structural regions, their arrangement, and responsive layout. No real content. Renders at least one organism. |
18	| **Page** | A **template instance** with real content applied. Defines the section arrangement within the primary content region for a specific page type. |
19	
20	> The boundary is set by what a component's template renders *itself*, recorded
21	> as `composes: [...]` in the contract. An atom has `composes: []`.
22	> Templates and pages are not recorded in the contract and are not delivered
23	> as Custom Elements. See Rule F.
24	
25	---
26	
27	## Rule A: icons are attributes, not components
28	
29	A glyph is delivered by an **attribute value** (e.g. `icon="arrow-right"`), never
30	by composing a separate Icon component. A component that accepts an icon attribute
31	composes nothing for that icon.
32	
33	- A Button with a leading icon → still an **atom** (icon is an attribute, not a composed component).
34	- Only a standalone displayed glyph is the `Icon` atom itself.
35	
36	---
37	
38	## Rule B: slot ≠ import
39	
40	A component passed **in** as slotted content does **not** change the parent's tier.
41	Only what the parent's own template renders itself counts.
42	
43	- A container that merely *holds* slotted children stays at its own tier.
44	- A Card that renders a CardHeader molecule in its own template → **organism**,
45	  regardless of what is slotted into its body.
46	
47	---
48	
49	## Rule C: Template defines structure, not content
50	
51	A template establishes the page frame and the positions of its structural regions.
52	It contains no real copy, imagery, or data. If a Figma frame contains real content,
53	it is a Page, not a Template.
54	
55	- A frame with a nav region, a grey placeholder hero, and a footer region → **Template**.
56	- The same frame with a real headline, product image, and body copy → **Page**.
57	
58	---
59	
60	## Rule D: Page is always an instance of a template
61	
62	Every page type belongs to exactly one template. Multiple page types can share the
63	same template shell. A new page type is only warranted when the section arrangement
64	within the primary content region differs materially from an existing one.
65	
66	- "About Us" and "About Us - History" sharing the same section rhythm → same page type, same template.
67	- "Offerings" with a fundamentally different section arrangement → separate page type.
68	
69	---
70	
71	## Rule E: Layout sections are not components
72	
73	Blocks and sections within the primary content region are layout instructions:
74	spacing, background colour, and container-query responsive sizing. They do not
75	receive contract entries unless they render component content themselves. Classify
76	them by structural role, not visual scale.
77	
78	---
79	
80	## Rule F: Templates and pages are not Custom Elements
81	
82	Templates and pages sit above the component delivery layer. They are
83	**spec-layer deliverables only**. They do not receive contract entries, do not
84	generate `.js` component files, and are not delivered as Custom Elements.
85	
86	The design system provides atoms, molecules, and organisms. How a developer
87	assembles those into a page frame within their stack (React layouts, Angular shell
88	components, LWC experience layers, vanilla HTML) is outside the scope of the
89	component library. A template spec communicates layout intent: the named regions,
90	which components live in each, and the responsive behaviour. Implementation is the
91	developer's decision.
92	
93	---
94	
95	## Edge tests (apply in this order)
96	
97	1. **Decorative internals are not components.** A badge dot, a toggle knob, a
98	   slider thumb: styled elements with no standalone identity. They do **not** bump
99	   the tier.
100	2. **Atom-only regions are molecules.** A top bar composing only Button + Logo →
101	   **molecule**, even though it spans the full viewport. Tier follows composition,
102	   not pixel size.
103	3. **Containers follow their template.** If a component's own template renders a
104	   molecule, it is an organism.
105	
106	---
107	
108	## Reading a Figma frame labelled as a template or page
109	
110	1. **Read structure first.** Identify the named structural regions in the frame,
111	   their vertical order, nesting depth, and responsive or breakpoint intent.
112	
113	2. **Map regions to semantic HTML.** Designers are not required to use HTML element
114	   names. The agent infers the semantic mapping from layer name and position.
115	   Common mappings:
116	
117	   | Figma layer name (examples) | Semantic element |
118	   |---|---|
119	   | Nav, Navigation, Nav Bar, Global Nav | `<nav>` |
120	   | Header, Site Header, Masthead | `<header>` |
121	   | Announcement Bar, Alert Bar, Promo Band | `<div>` or `<aside>` (above `<header>`) |
122	   | Hero, Page Hero, Banner | `<section>` (within `<main>`) |
123	   | Content Area, Main Content, Body | `<main>` |
124	   | Sidebar, Side Nav, Aside | `<aside>` |
125	   | Footer, Site Footer, Footer Links | `<footer>` |
126	
127	3. **Flag ambiguous names before assigning.** If a region name carries no functional
128	   signal (e.g. "Blue Bar", "Wide Strip"), stop and ask before assigning a semantic
129	   element.
130	
131	4. **Then read composition.** Once regions are mapped, identify which organisms,
132	   molecules, or atoms appear within each region.
133	
134	5. **Determine tier by content.** Placeholder text and grey boxes → Template.
135	   Real copy and imagery → Page. For frames with mixed content (some regions
136	   real, some placeholder), classify by the majority: if most regions carry real
137	   content, classify as Page; if most are placeholder, classify as Template. Note
138	   the ambiguity in the spec's Overview section so the designer can verify.
139	
140	6. **Note repeating sections.** Layout sections that repeat across subpages of the
141	   same type define the page type's identity. Document them in the spec as
142	   page-type structure, not as individual components.
143	
144	---
145	
146	## When you need something new
147	
148	If a component or variant is not in the contract, **STOP and flag it** as a
149	proposed contract addition. Do not invent a component outside the contract.
150	Adding it means: a new contract entry + the tier decided by these rules +
151	implementation as a Custom Element. This applies to atoms, molecules, and organisms
152	only. Templates and pages are never added to the contract.
153

every component at the atom, molecule, and organism level only.

---

## The five tiers

|---|---|

| **Template** | Defines the **skeletal page frame**: a set of named structural regions, their arrangement, and responsive layout. No real content. Renders at least one organism. |
| **Page** | A **template instance** with real content applied. Defines the section arrangement within the primary content region for a specific page type. |

> The boundary is set by what a component's template renders *itself*, recorded
> as `composes: [...]` in the contract. An atom has `composes: []`.
> Templates and pages are not recorded in the contract and are not delivered
> as Custom Elements. See Rule F.

---

## Rule A: icons are attributes, not components

A glyph is delivered by an **attribute value** (e.g. `icon="arrow-right"`), never
by composing a separate Icon component. A component that accepts an icon attribute
composes nothing for that icon.

- A Button with a leading icon → still an **atom** (icon is an attribute, not a composed component).
- Only a standalone displayed glyph is the `Icon` atom itself.

---

## Rule B: slot ≠ import

A component passed **in** as slotted content does **not** change the parent's tier.
Only what the parent's own template renders itself counts.

- A container that merely *holds* slotted children stays at its own tier.
- A Card that renders a CardHeader molecule in its own template → **organism**,
  regardless of what is slotted into its body.

---

## Rule C: Template defines structure, not content

A template establishes the page frame and the positions of its structural regions.
It contains no real copy, imagery, or data. If a Figma frame contains real content,
it is a Page, not a Template.

- A frame with a nav region, a grey placeholder hero, and a footer region → **Template**.
- The same frame with a real headline, product image, and body copy → **Page**.

---

## Rule D: Page is always an instance of a template

Every page type belongs to exactly one template. Multiple page types can share the
same template shell. A new page type is only warranted when the section arrangement
within the primary content region differs materially from an existing one.

- "About Us" and "About Us - History" sharing the same section rhythm → same page type, same template.
- "Offerings" with a fundamentally different section arrangement → separate page type.

---

## Rule E: Layout sections are not components

Blocks and sections within the primary content region are layout instructions:
spacing, background colour, and container-query responsive sizing. They do not
receive contract entries unless they render component content themselves. Classify
them by structural role, not visual scale.

---

## Rule F: Templates and pages are not Custom Elements

Templates and pages sit above the component delivery layer. They are
**spec-layer deliverables only**. They do not receive contract entries, do not
generate `.js` component files, and are not delivered as Custom Elements.

The design system provides atoms, molecules, and organisms. How a developer
assembles those into a page frame within their stack (React layouts, Angular shell
components, LWC experience layers, vanilla HTML) is outside the scope of the
component library. A template spec communicates layout intent: the named regions,
which components live in each, and the responsive behaviour. Implementation is the
developer's decision.

---

## Edge tests (apply in this order)

1. **Decorative internals are not components.** A badge dot, a toggle knob, a
   slider thumb: styled elements with no standalone identity. They do **not** bump
   the tier.
2. **Atom-only regions are molecules.** A top bar composing only Button + Logo →
   **molecule**, even though it spans the full viewport. Tier follows composition,
   not pixel size.
3. **Containers follow their template.** If a component's own template renders a
   molecule, it is an organism.

---

## Reading a Figma frame labelled as a template or page

1. **Read structure first.** Identify the named structural regions in the frame,
   their vertical order, nesting depth, and responsive or breakpoint intent.

2. **Map regions to semantic HTML.** Designers are not required to use HTML element
   names. The agent infers the semantic mapping from layer name and position.
   Common mappings:

   | Figma layer name (examples) | Semantic element |
   |---|---|
   | Nav, Navigation, Nav Bar, Global Nav | `<nav>` |
   | Header, Site Header, Masthead | `<header>` |
   | Announcement Bar, Alert Bar, Promo Band | `<div>` or `<aside>` (above `<header>`) |
   | Hero, Page Hero, Banner | `<section>` (within `<main>`) |
   | Content Area, Main Content, Body | `<main>` |
   | Sidebar, Side Nav, Aside | `<aside>` |
   | Footer, Site Footer, Footer Links | `<footer>` |

3. **Flag ambiguous names before assigning.** If a region name carries no functional
   signal (e.g. "Blue Bar", "Wide Strip"), stop and ask before assigning a semantic
   element.

4. **Then read composition.** Once regions are mapped, identify which organisms,
   molecules, or atoms appear within each region.

5. **Determine tier by content.** Placeholder text and grey boxes → Template.
   Real copy and imagery → Page. For frames with mixed content (some regions
   real, some placeholder), classify by the majority: if most regions carry real
   content, classify as Page; if most are placeholder, classify as Template. Note
   the ambiguity in the spec's Overview section so the designer can verify.

6. **Note repeating sections.** Layout sections that repeat across subpages of the
   same type define the page type's identity. Document them in the spec as
   page-type structure, not as individual components.

---

## When you need something new

If a component or variant is not in the contract, **STOP and flag it** as a
proposed contract addition. Do not invent a component outside the contract.
Adding it means: a new contract entry + the tier decided by these rules +
implementation as a Custom Element. This applies to atoms, molecules, and organisms
only. Templates and pages are never added to the contract.

2	
3	Read this during the path resolution pre-flight of any skill. Resolves ADW paths from project config and handles missing structure gracefully.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Step 1: Resolve paths
8	
9	Check for `project.config.js` at the repo root.
10	
11	- If found: read it. If a `paths` object is present, use those values to override the defaults below. Keys not present in `paths` fall back to ADW defaults.
12	- If not found: use ADW defaults for all paths. Note in context that this may not be an ADW project.
13	
14	**Default paths (override via `paths` in `project.config.js`):**
15	
16	| Config key | Default path |
17	|---|---|
18	| `contextRoot` | `01-context` |
19	| `contextProject` | `01-context/project-context.md` |
20	| `contextDecisions` | `01-context/decisions.md` |
21	| `contextSummaries` | `01-context/summaries` |
22	| `contextDiscovery` | `01-context/discovery` |
23	| `contextRefsLocal` | `01-context/ref-local` |
24	| `contextRefsExt` | `01-context/ref-external` |
25	| `design` | `02-design` |
26	| `library` | `02-design/library` |
27	| `libraryTokens` | `02-design/library/tokens.md` |
28	| `libraryCss` | `02-design/library/common.css` |
29	| `libraryElements` | `02-design/library/elements` |
30	| `specs` | `02-design/specs` |
31	| `prototypes` | `02-design/prototypes` |
32	| `viewer` | `02-design/viewer` |
33	| `requirements` | `03-requirements` |
34	| `feedback` | `04-feedback` |
35	| `handover` | `05-handover` |
36	
37	---
38	
39	## Step 2: Check required paths
40	
41	For each path marked **Required** in the calling skill's pre-flight: check whether it exists at the resolved location.
42	
43	If one or more required paths are missing, stop and surface them before proceeding:
44	
45	> "[skill name]: Some required paths are missing.
46	>
47	> Missing:
48	> - `[resolved path]`
49	>
50	> How would you like to proceed?
51	> (a) Create the standard ADW folder structure for the missing paths
52	> (b) Point me to your existing locations (used for this session only, not saved)
53	> (c) Continue without them (this skill will run in limited mode, some features unavailable)
54	>
55	> You can also run `/setup` to permanently map your project structure to ADW conventions."
56	
57	Wait for the user's response before proceeding.
58	
59	- **(a) Create:** create the missing folders and any required stub files at their ADW default paths. If `project.config.js` does not exist, offer to create a minimal one.
60	- **(b) Redirect:** ask for each missing path one at a time. Store the custom locations in context for this session only.
61	- **(c) Continue:** note which features are unavailable. Proceed with what exists.
62

66

68	
69	---
70	
71	## Step 4: Return
72	
73	All path resolution is complete. Proceed with the calling skill using resolved paths throughout. Do not use hardcoded ADW defaults after this point if overrides were found.

1	# Skill: /capture-feedback
2	
3	Extracts all comments from the project Figma file (resolved and unresolved) and writes them to `/04-feedback/` as a structured markdown document grouped by frame. Uses the Figma REST API directly via WebFetch. No extra installation required.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Pre-flight checks
8	
9	1. Read `CLAUDE.local.md` and extract the Figma Personal Access Token.
10	   - If missing: "Add your Figma Personal Access Token to CLAUDE.local.md under 'Figma credentials'. Generate one at figma.com → Settings → Personal access tokens. This is the only skill that needs it."
11	
12	2. Ask: "Paste the URL of the Figma design file you want to pull comments from."
13	
14	3. Extract the file key from the URL:
15	   - URL format: `https://www.figma.com/file/[KEY]/...` or `https://www.figma.com/design/[KEY]/...`
16	   - The key is the first path segment after `/file/` or `/design/`
17	
18	---
19	
20	## Pre-flight: Path resolution
21	
22	Read `.claude/skills/_shared/portability.md` and resolve paths before scanning.
23	
24	Required: `feedback`
25	
26	---
27	
28	## Step 1: Fetch all comments
29	
30	Make a GET request:
31	
32	```
33	GET https://api.figma.com/v1/files/{key}/comments
34	Headers: X-Figma-Token: {token}
35	```
36	
37	Parse the response. Each comment object includes:
38	
39	| Field | Description |
40	|---|---|
41	| `id` | Unique comment ID |
42	| `message` | The comment text |
43	| `user.handle` | Author's Figma username |
44	| `created_at` | ISO 8601 timestamp |
45	| `resolved_at` | ISO 8601 timestamp if resolved, otherwise null |
46	| `client_meta.node_id` | ID of the anchored frame/layer, if any. Absent for canvas-level comments. |
47	
48	Separate comments into two groups:
49	- **Anchored:** `client_meta.node_id` is present
50	- **Unanchored:** no `client_meta.node_id` (canvas-level or global)
51	
52	If the response contains zero comments, stop and say: "No comments found in this Figma file. The file may have no comments, or your token may not have access."
53	
54	---
55	
56	## Step 2: Resolve frame names
57	
58	Collect all unique `node_id` values from anchored comments. Make a single GET request:
59	
60	```
61	GET https://api.figma.com/v1/files/{key}/nodes?ids={comma-separated-node-ids}
62	Headers: X-Figma-Token: {token}
63	```
64	
65	Build a map of `node_id → name` from `response.nodes[id].document.name`.
66	
67	If a node_id cannot be resolved (e.g. the frame was deleted): use the node_id itself as the section heading, suffixed with `(deleted frame)`.
68	
69	---
70	
71	## Step 3: Collate by frame
72	
73	Group anchored comments by frame name. Sort comments within each group by `created_at` ascending (oldest first).
74	
75	Sort frames alphabetically by name.
76	
77	---
78	
79	## Step 4: Write output file
80	
81	Create `/04-feedback/YYYY-MM-DD-figma-comments.md` (today's date). If a file for today already exists, append `-2`, `-3`, etc.
82	
83	Use this structure:
84	
85	```markdown
86	<!-- changelog
87	YYYY-MM-DD | /capture-feedback | N comments across N frames (N resolved)
88	Full history: GitHub → 04-feedback/YYYY-MM-DD-figma-comments.md → History
89	-->
90	
91	# Figma Feedback: [project from project.config.js]
92	
93	**Source:** Figma comments only. Prototype feedback is a separate workflow.
94	**Captured:** YYYY-MM-DD
95	**Figma file:** [Figma file URL]
96	**Total comments:** N (N open, N resolved)
97	
98	---
99	
100	## [Frame Name]
101	
102	| # | Author | Date | Time (AEST/AEDT) | Status | Comment |
103	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
104	| 1 | username | DD Mon YYYY | HH:MM | Open | Comment text |
105	| 2 | username | DD Mon YYYY | HH:MM | Resolved | Comment text |
106	
107	---
108	
109	## [Next Frame Name]
110	
111	...
112	
113	---
114	
115	## Canvas-level (no frame anchor)
116	
117	| # | Author | Date | Time (AEST/AEDT) | Status | Comment |
118	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
119	```
120	
121	**Formatting rules:**
122	- Date: Australian format, DD Mon YYYY (e.g. 15 Jan 2025)
123	- Time: Convert UTC timestamps to AEST (UTC+10) or AEDT (UTC+11) depending on DST. Label the column accordingly.
124	- Status: "Open" if `resolved_at` is null, "Resolved" if not.
125	- Comment text: escape any pipe `|` characters in comments with `\|` to preserve table formatting.
126	- If a frame has no comments after filtering, omit it.
127	- Omit the "Canvas-level" section if there are no unanchored comments.
128	
129	---
130	
131	## Step 5: Done
132	
133	Tell the user the file written and the comment/frame count. No further action.
134

1	# Skill: /deploy-catalog
2	
3	Publishes the component catalog to a live URL so developers and stakeholders can browse components, their APIs, and live demos without cloning the repo. The catalog reads `[prefix]-contract.js` directly, so it stays up to date with every push.
4	
5	The catalog is deployed as a route (`/catalog`) on the existing Vercel project, not as a separate deployment. Run `/deploy-viewer` first if you have not deployed to Vercel yet. This skill extends that same project.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Pre-flight checks
10	
11	1. Read `project.config.js`. Get `componentPrefix`, `catalog.deployUrl` (if set), and `viewer.deployUrl` (to detect existing Vercel project).
12	2. Check that `02-design/catalog/index.html` exists. If not, stop: "The catalog shell is missing at `02-design/catalog/index.html`. Run `/extract` to populate at least one component and re-run this skill."
13	3. Check that `02-design/library/contract/[prefix]-contract.js` exists and exports a non-empty `contract` array. If empty or missing, warn: "The contract is empty. The catalog will deploy but will show no components until you run `/extract` to populate it."
14	4. If `catalog.deployUrl` is already set in `project.config.js`, ask: "The catalog is already live at [URL]. Do you want to redeploy or just push an update?"
15	   - If redeploy: confirm and continue from Step 1.
16	   - If push update: jump to Step 3 (push only).
17	
18	---
19	
20	## Step 1: Verify vercel.json
21	
22	Read `vercel.json` in the repo root. It must include a rewrite rule for `/catalog`:
23	
24	```json
25	{
26	  "rewrites": [
27	    { "source": "/", "destination": "/02-design/viewer/index.html" },
28	    { "source": "/catalog", "destination": "/02-design/catalog/index.html" },
29	    { "source": "/catalog/(.*)", "destination": "/02-design/catalog/index.html" }
30	  ]
31	}
32	```
33	
34	Check whether the `/catalog` rules are already there:
35	- If yes: continue.
36	- If no: add them. Do not remove or alter existing rules.
37	
38	If the viewer rewrite (`"source": "/"`) is not in the file yet (i.e. `/deploy-viewer` has not been run), add it too:
39	
40	```json
41	{
42	  "rewrites": [
43	    { "source": "/", "destination": "/02-design/viewer/index.html" },
44	    { "source": "/catalog", "destination": "/02-design/catalog/index.html" },
45	    { "source": "/catalog/(.*)", "destination": "/02-design/catalog/index.html" }
46	  ]
47	}
48	```
49	
50	Tell the user: "Updated `vercel.json` with the `/catalog` route."
51	
52	---
53	
54	## Step 2: Vercel project check
55	
56	Check whether a Vercel project is already connected (look for `viewer.deployUrl` in `project.config.js`):
57	
58	- **Existing Vercel project:** The catalog will deploy automatically on next push. Tell the user:
59	  > "Your project is already on Vercel at [viewer.deployUrl]. Adding the `/catalog` route; the catalog will be live at `[viewer.deployUrl]/catalog` after this push. No extra Vercel setup needed."
60	  Jump to Step 3.
61	
62	- **No existing Vercel project:** The user needs to connect to Vercel first. Tell them:
63	  > "Your project is not on Vercel yet. To deploy the catalog (and the viewer), you need to connect this repo to Vercel first. Run `/deploy-viewer`; it handles the full Vercel setup and the catalog route will be included."
64	  Stop here. The user should run `/deploy-viewer`, which now includes the catalog route in vercel.json.
65	
66	---
67	
68	## Step 3: Commit and push
69	
70	Stage and commit the updated files:
71	
72	```
73	git add vercel.json
74	git commit -m "Add component catalog route"

# Skill: /deploy-catalog

Publishes the component catalog to a live URL so developers and stakeholders can browse components, their APIs, and live demos without cloning the repo. The catalog reads `[prefix]-contract.js` directly, so it stays up to date with every push.

The catalog is deployed as a route (`/catalog`) on the existing Vercel project, not as a separate deployment. Run `/deploy-viewer` first if you have not deployed to Vercel yet. This skill extends that same project.

---

## Pre-flight checks

1. Read `project.config.js`. Get `componentPrefix`, `catalog.deployUrl` (if set), and `viewer.deployUrl` (to detect existing Vercel project).
2. Check that `02-design/catalog/index.html` exists. If not, stop: "The catalog shell is missing at `02-design/catalog/index.html`. Run `/extract` to populate at least one component and re-run this skill."
3. Check that `02-design/library/contract/[prefix]-contract.js` exists and exports a non-empty `contract` array. If empty or missing, warn: "The contract is empty. The catalog will deploy but will show no components until you run `/extract` to populate it."
4. If `catalog.deployUrl` is already set in `project.config.js`, ask: "The catalog is already live at [URL]. Do you want to redeploy or just push an update?"
   - If redeploy: confirm and continue from Step 1.
   - If push update: jump to Step 3 (push only).

---

## Step 1: Verify vercel.json

Read `vercel.json` in the repo root. It must include a rewrite rule for `/catalog`:

```json
{
  "rewrites": [
    { "source": "/", "destination": "/02-design/viewer/index.html" },
    { "source": "/catalog", "destination": "/02-design/catalog/index.html" },
    { "source": "/catalog/(.*)", "destination": "/02-design/catalog/index.html" }
  ]
}
```

Check whether the `/catalog` rules are already there:
- If yes: continue.
- If no: add them. Do not remove or alter existing rules.

If the viewer rewrite (`"source": "/"`) is not in the file yet (i.e. `/deploy-viewer` has not been run), add it too:

```json
{
  "rewrites": [
    { "source": "/", "destination": "/02-design/viewer/index.html" },
    { "source": "/catalog", "destination": "/02-design/catalog/index.html" },
    { "source": "/catalog/(.*)", "destination": "/02-design/catalog/index.html" }
  ]
}
```

Tell the user: "Updated `vercel.json` with the `/catalog` route."

---

## Step 2: Vercel project check

Check whether a Vercel project is already connected (look for `viewer.deployUrl` in `project.config.js`):

- **Existing Vercel project:** The catalog will deploy automatically on next push. Tell the user:
  > "Your project is already on Vercel at [viewer.deployUrl]. Adding the `/catalog` route; the catalog will be live at `[viewer.deployUrl]/catalog` after this push. No extra Vercel setup needed."
  Jump to Step 3.

- **No existing Vercel project:** The user needs to connect to Vercel first. Tell them:
  > "Your project is not on Vercel yet. To deploy the catalog (and the viewer), you need to connect this repo to Vercel first. Run `/deploy-viewer`; it handles the full Vercel setup and the catalog route will be included."
  Stop here. The user should run `/deploy-viewer`, which now includes the catalog route in vercel.json.

---

## Step 3: Commit and push

Stage and commit the updated files:

```
git add vercel.json
git commit -m "Add component catalog route"
git push
```

Tell the user: "Pushed. Vercel is now deploying; it usually takes under 60 seconds."

---

## Step 4: Derive the catalog URL

The catalog URL is the existing Vercel deployment URL with `/catalog` appended:

```
[viewer.deployUrl]/catalog
```

Example: `https://my-project.vercel.app/catalog`

---

## Step 5: Record the URL

Write the catalog URL to `project.config.js`:

```js
catalog: {
  deployUrl: "https://my-project.vercel.app/catalog",
},
```

If a `catalog:` block already exists, update `deployUrl` only. If it does not exist, add it after `viewer:`.

Commit and push:

```
git add project.config.js
git commit -m "Record catalog deployment URL"
git push
```

---

## Step 6: Update handover index

If `05-handover/index.md` exists, check whether it has a catalog link under the **Components** section. If the link is missing or stale, update it:

```markdown
Browse live: [Component catalog](https://my-project.vercel.app/catalog)
```

Commit if changed:

```
git add 05-handover/index.md
git commit -m "Update catalog link in handover index"
git push
```

---

## Step 7: Confirm

Tell the user:

- Catalog live at: `[catalog.deployUrl]`
- The catalog reads `[prefix]-contract.js` directly. Re-running `/extract` and pushing updates the catalog automatically, no extra steps
- Share [catalog.deployUrl] with the dev team as part of the handover package
- The catalog URL is also in `05-handover/index.md` under Components

1	# Skill: /extract
2	
3	Single entry point for all design extraction. Identifies what you have, explains what it will produce, and routes to the right process. Replaces `/extract-library`, `/extract-specs`, and `/extract-interaction`.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Pre-flight: Check for incomplete sessions
8	
9	Check memory for any incomplete `/extract` session. If found, surface it first:
10	> "[date]: An /extract session was not completed. Continue where you left off?"
11	Wait for response before proceeding.
12	
13	---
14	
15	## Pre-flight: Path resolution
16	
17	Read `.claude/skills/_shared/portability.md` and resolve paths before scanning.
18	
19	Required: `library`, `specs`
20	Optional: `contextProject`, `prototypes`
21	
22	---
23	
24	## Step 1: Get the source
25	
26	Write a memory entry: "Skill /extract started [today's date], incomplete."
27	
28	Ask: "Paste a Figma link, a URL (Storybook or live site), a local file path (JSON, CSS, SCSS, or Markdown), or type a prototype folder name. Say 'everything' to run a full extraction pass on all Figma sources."
29	
30	---
31	
32	## Step 2: Identify the source
33	
34	Analyse what was pasted or typed. For Figma URLs, use the Figma MCP to read the frame structure before classifying.
35	
36	**The distinction "library file vs design file" does not apply.** Any Figma file can be the source for tokens, components, or both. The frame's content determines the route — not the file it lives in.
37	
38	| What was given | How to identify | Routes to |
39	|---|---|---|
40	| Figma tokens/styles frame | Frame contains colour swatches, typography scales, spacing values, or variable definitions. Primarily reference content with no interactive component set. | `library.md` (tokens mode) |
41	| Figma component frame | Named, bounded UI unit with variants, states, or a component set | Reusability assessment (see below) |
42	| Figma template or page frame | Full-screen layout with named structural regions (header, main, footer, or equivalent). Use Figma MCP to read the frame: placeholder content → Template; real content → Page. | `specs.md` (template) |
43	| Figma screen frame | Content-bearing UI screen or state — not a full page shell with structural regions. | `specs.md` (screen) |
44	| Figma flow frame | Flow or journey layout connecting multiple screens. | `specs.md` (flow) |
45	| Prototype folder name or path | Matches an existing folder under `/02-design/prototypes/`. Read its `intent.md` to check the `stage` field, then ask: "Interaction spec, template spec, or component/screen spec?" | `interaction.md` for interaction; `specs.md` (template) for `stage: template`; `specs.md` (Path B) for component or screen |
46	| Storybook URL | `https://` URL pointing to a hosted Storybook | `non-figma.md` (tokens) |
47	| Live website URL | `https://` URL pointing to a live site (not Figma, not Storybook). Ask: "Are you extracting tokens or documenting this as a spec?" | `non-figma.md` for tokens, `specs.md` (Path C) for spec |
48	| Image file (.png, .jpg) | Path to a local image file | `specs.md` (Path C), converted via MarkItDown (with OCR) if needed |
49	| PDF file | Path to a local PDF | `specs.md` (Path C), converted via MarkItDown |
50	| Word/Excel/PowerPoint (.docx, .xlsx, .pptx) | Path to a document file | `specs.md` (Path C), converted via MarkItDown |
51	| JSON token file | Path to a `.json` file (Design Tokens, Style Dictionary, or custom format) | `non-figma.md` (tokens) |
52	| CSS or SCSS file | Path to a `.css` or `.scss` file | `non-figma.md` (tokens) |
53	| Markdown file | Path to a `.md` file containing token or component documentation | `non-figma.md` (tokens) |
54	| Written description or whiteboard photo | Plain text description or image of a sketch with no design tool source | `specs.md` (Path D) |
55	| "everything", "all", or no specific source | User wants a full extraction pass | Confirm, then run `library.md` (tokens) → `library.md` Mode C for each component frame → `interaction.md` (all prototypes) in sequence |
56	
57	### Reusability assessment (component frames)
58	
59	When a Figma frame is identified as a component frame, run this assessment before routing.
60	
61	**Default assumption: it is reusable.** Any named, bounded UI component is a library candidate. The designer opts out rather than in.
62	
63	**Determine the atomic tier** from the frame's layer structure and child components:
64	
65	| Tier | Characteristics | Examples |
66	|---|---|---|
67	| Atom | Single-purpose unit. No sub-components. Renders one thing. | Button, icon, input field, badge, tag, price label, avatar, checkbox, radio |
68	| Molecule | 2–5 atoms combined into one functional unit with a clear single job. | Search field, nav item, product card, form group, icon button, rating, wishlist toggle |
69	| Organism | Complex section with its own layout, composed of molecules and/or atoms. Occupies a full region of a page. | Navigation bar, site header, site footer, product grid, cart panel, mega menu, filter sidebar |
70	
71	Read the frame structure: layer names, child component instances, and layout dimensions. Pick the lowest tier that fits — don't over-promote.
72	
73	**Surface the proposal:**
74	
75	> "This looks like a [tier] — [one-line description of what it does and where it appears in a real build]. I'll extract it as a library element (Web Component + demo at `02-design/library/elements/[name]/`) and write a spec (`02-design/specs/components/[name].md`). That makes it usable in prototypes and ready for dev handover. Sound right, or should this be spec-only?"
76	
77	Wait for the designer's response.
78	
79	- **Confirmed (or any affirmative):** Route to `library.md` Mode C. One pass produces the library element and the spec.
80	- **Wrong tier:** Designer corrects the tier. Update and proceed.
81	- **Spec-only:** Route to `specs.md` Path A. No library element written.
82	
83	---
84	
85	## Step 3: Explain in plain English
86	
87	Tell the user what you found and what you are about to produce. Keep it simple. Junior designers are the audience. Avoid jargon unless the user has clearly demonstrated familiarity.
88	
89	**Figma component frame (reusable — library element + spec):**
90	> "That's a [tier] — [what it does]. I'll build it as a Web Component so it's usable in any prototype, and write a spec so developers can implement it. Files go into `02-design/library/elements/[name]/` and `02-design/specs/components/[name].md`."
91	
92	**Figma component frame (spec-only):**
93	> "That's a component design. I'll document how it's built, what states and variants it has, and grab a screenshot. Output goes into `02-design/specs/components/`."
94	
95	**Figma tokens/styles frame:**
96	> "That's your tokens/styles reference. I'll document all the colour, spacing, and typography values and write them as CSS custom properties. Output goes into `02-design/library/tokens.md` and `02-design/library/common.css`."
97	
98	**Figma template or page frame:**
99	> "That's a [template / page]. I'll document the structural regions, component mapping per region, and responsive layout behaviour. Output goes into `02-design/specs/templates/`."
100	
101	**Figma screen frame:**
102	> "That's a screen design. I'll document the layout, content, styles used, and interactive elements, and take a screenshot. Output goes into `02-design/specs/screens/`."
103	
104	**Figma flow frame:**
105	> "That's a flow or navigation design. I'll document the screens, transitions, and connection logic, and take a screenshot. Output goes into `02-design/specs/flows/`."
106	
107	**Prototype folder:**
108	> "That's the [folder name] prototype. I'll extract the interaction specs and update the linked spec file. I'll also check for any new styles that should be promoted to the shared library."
109	
110	**Non-Figma source (Storybook URL, live site, JSON, CSS, SCSS, Markdown):**
111	> "That's a [source type]. I'll extract what I can: colours, typography, spacing, and any other named values. For URLs, expect some noise — I can only read what's publicly visible and can't always tell intentional tokens from utility styles or third-party injections. Everything starts as a candidate. You review, confirm, and I publish to `/02-design/library/`."
112	
113	**Prototype (spec extraction):**
114	> "That's the [folder name] prototype. I'll check if a spec already exists for it. If it does, I'll point you there. If not, I'll read the code and produce a [component / screen / template] spec: token references, structure, behaviour intent, and any responsive layout notes from the prototype's intent file."
115	
116	**Image, PDF, or live URL (spec extraction):**
117	> "That's a [image / PDF / URL]. I'll analyse what's visible and produce a spec with approximate layout, colours, and component structure. Values I can't measure precisely will be flagged as estimated. Same spec format, but treat flagged values as starting points to verify."
118	
119	**Written description or whiteboard photo:**
120	> "Got it. No visual design values to extract here, so I'll produce a behaviour-focused spec: what the component or screen does, its states, variants, and any accessibility intent. Token values and layout will be left blank for a designer to fill in."
121	
122	Then ask: "Is that what you're trying to do, or something different?"
123	
124	---
125	
126	## Step 4: Argue if intent doesn't match source
127	
128	If the user confirms something that does not match what the source can produce, push back clearly. One push-back is enough. If the user insists after the explanation, proceed with their stated intent.
129	
130	Examples:
131	- User pastes a component frame link but says they want tokens: "That link is a component, not a styles/variables frame. You won't get tokens from it — you'd get a library element and spec. Did you mean to paste your tokens frame link instead?"
132	- User names a prototype folder but says they want a component spec: "That's a local prototype folder, not a Figma frame. I can extract interaction specs from it, but not a component spec. For a component spec, paste a Figma link to the component frame instead."
133	- User pastes a screen frame but says they want a library element: "That link points to a screen, not a component. I can extract a screen spec from it, but not a library element. Paste a link to the specific component frame you want extracted."
134	
135	---
136	
137	## Step 5: Route
138	
139	Once source and intent are confirmed, read and follow the instructions in the appropriate sub-file:
140	
141	- **Reusable component (library element + spec):** read `.claude/skills/extract/library.md` and follow all steps (Mode C)
142	- **Tokens/styles extraction:** read `.claude/skills/extract/library.md` and follow all steps (Mode A or B)
143	- **Spec-only (screens, templates, flows, or spec-only components):** read `.claude/skills/extract/specs.md` and follow all steps
144	- **Interaction extraction:** read `.claude/skills/extract/interaction.md` and follow all steps
145	- **Non-Figma extraction:** read `.claude/skills/extract/non-figma.md` and follow all steps
146	- **Full pass:** run `library.md` (tokens, if a tokens frame exists or was identified) → `library.md` Mode C for each component frame found → `interaction.md` (all prototypes in `/02-design/prototypes/`) in sequence
147	
148	---
149	
150	## Step 6: Complete
151	
152	Update the memory entry to: "Skill /extract completed [today's date]."
153

Analyse what was pasted or typed. For Figma URLs, use the Figma MCP to read the frame structure before classifying.

**The distinction "library file vs design file" does not apply.** Any Figma file can be the source for tokens, components, or both. The frame's content determines the route — not the file it lives in.

| What was given | How to identify | Routes to |
|---|---|---|
| Figma tokens/styles frame | Frame contains colour swatches, typography scales, spacing values, or variable definitions. Primarily reference content with no interactive component set. | `library.md` (tokens mode) |
| Figma component frame | Named, bounded UI unit with variants, states, or a component set | Reusability assessment (see below) |
| Figma template or page frame | Full-screen layout with named structural regions (header, main, footer, or equivalent). Use Figma MCP to read the frame: placeholder content → Template; real content → Page. | `specs.md` (template) |
| Figma screen frame | Content-bearing UI screen or state — not a full page shell with structural regions. | `specs.md` (screen) |
| Figma flow frame | Flow or journey layout connecting multiple screens. | `specs.md` (flow) |
| Prototype folder name or path | Matches an existing folder under `/02-design/prototypes/`. Read its `intent.md` to check the `stage` field, then ask: "Interaction spec, template spec, or component/screen spec?" | `interaction.md` for interaction; `specs.md` (template) for `stage: template`; `specs.md` (Path B) for component or screen |
| Storybook URL | `https://` URL pointing to a hosted Storybook | `non-figma.md` (tokens) |
| Live website URL | `https://` URL pointing to a live site (not Figma, not Storybook). Ask: "Are you extracting tokens or documenting this as a spec?" | `non-figma.md` for tokens, `specs.md` (Path C) for spec |
| Image file (.png, .jpg) | Path to a local image file | `specs.md` (Path C), converted via MarkItDown (with OCR) if needed |
| PDF file | Path to a local PDF | `specs.md` (Path C), converted via MarkItDown |
| Word/Excel/PowerPoint (.docx, .xlsx, .pptx) | Path to a document file | `specs.md` (Path C), converted via MarkItDown |
| JSON token file | Path to a `.json` file (Design Tokens, Style Dictionary, or custom format) | `non-figma.md` (tokens) |
| CSS or SCSS file | Path to a `.css` or `.scss` file | `non-figma.md` (tokens) |
| Markdown file | Path to a `.md` file containing token or component documentation | `non-figma.md` (tokens) |
| Written description or whiteboard photo | Plain text description or image of a sketch with no design tool source | `specs.md` (Path D) |
| "everything", "all", or no specific source | User wants a full extraction pass | Confirm, then run `library.md` (tokens) → `library.md` Mode C for each component frame → `interaction.md` (all prototypes) in sequence |

### Reusability assessment (component frames)

When a Figma frame is identified as a component frame, run this assessment before routing.

**Default assumption: it is reusable.** Any named, bounded UI component is a library candidate. The designer opts out rather than in.

**Determine the atomic tier** from the frame's layer structure and child components:

| Tier | Characteristics | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| Atom | Single-purpose unit. No sub-components. Renders one thing. | Button, icon, input field, badge, tag, price label, avatar, checkbox, radio |
| Molecule | 2–5 atoms combined into one functional unit with a clear single job. | Search field, nav item, product card, form group, icon button, rating, wishlist toggle |
| Organism | Complex section with its own layout, composed of molecules and/or atoms. Occupies a full region of a page. | Navigation bar, site header, site footer, product grid, cart panel, mega menu, filter sidebar |

Read the frame structure: layer names, child component instances, and layout dimensions. Pick the lowest tier that fits — don't over-promote.

**Surface the proposal:**

> "This looks like a [tier] — [one-line description of what it does and where it appears in a real build]. I'll extract it as a library element (Web Component + demo at `02-design/library/elements/[name]/`) and write a spec (`02-design/specs/components/[name].md`). That makes it usable in prototypes and ready for dev handover. Sound right, or should this be spec-only?"

Wait for the designer's response.

- **Confirmed (or any affirmative):** Route to `library.md` Mode C. One pass produces the library element and the spec.
- **Wrong tier:** Designer corrects the tier. Update and proceed.
- **Spec-only:** Route to `specs.md` Path A. No library element written.

---

## Step 3: Explain in plain English

Tell the user what you found and what you are about to produce. Keep it simple. Junior designers are the audience. Avoid jargon unless the user has clearly demonstrated familiarity.

**Figma component frame (reusable — library element + spec):**
> "That's a [tier] — [what it does]. I'll build it as a Web Component so it's usable in any prototype, and write a spec so developers can implement it. Files go into `02-design/library/elements/[name]/` and `02-design/specs/components/[name].md`."

**Figma component frame (spec-only):**
> "That's a component design. I'll document how it's built, what states and variants it has, and grab a screenshot. Output goes into `02-design/specs/components/`."

**Figma tokens/styles frame:**
> "That's your tokens/styles reference. I'll document all the colour, spacing, and typography values and write them as CSS custom properties. Output goes into `02-design/library/tokens.md` and `02-design/library/common.css`."

**Figma template or page frame:**
> "That's a [template / page]. I'll document the structural regions, component mapping per region, and responsive layout behaviour. Output goes into `02-design/specs/templates/`."

**Figma screen frame:**
> "That's a screen design. I'll document the layout, content, styles used, and interactive elements, and take a screenshot. Output goes into `02-design/specs/screens/`."

**Figma flow frame:**
> "That's a flow or navigation design. I'll document the screens, transitions, and connection logic, and take a screenshot. Output goes into `02-design/specs/flows/`."

**Prototype folder:**
> "That's the [folder name] prototype. I'll extract the interaction specs and update the linked spec file. I'll also check for any new styles that should be promoted to the shared library."

**Non-Figma source (Storybook URL, live site, JSON, CSS, SCSS, Markdown):**
> "That's a [source type]. I'll extract what I can: colours, typography, spacing, and any other named values. For URLs, expect some noise — I can only read what's publicly visible and can't always tell intentional tokens from utility styles or third-party injections. Everything starts as a candidate. You review, confirm, and I publish to `/02-design/library/`."

**Prototype (spec extraction):**
> "That's the [folder name] prototype. I'll check if a spec already exists for it. If it does, I'll point you there. If not, I'll read the code and produce a [component / screen / template] spec: token references, structure, behaviour intent, and any responsive layout notes from the prototype's intent file."

**Image, PDF, or live URL (spec extraction):**
> "That's a [image / PDF / URL]. I'll analyse what's visible and produce a spec with approximate layout, colours, and component structure. Values I can't measure precisely will be flagged as estimated. Same spec format, but treat flagged values as starting points to verify."

**Written description or whiteboard photo:**
> "Got it. No visual design values to extract here, so I'll produce a behaviour-focused spec: what the component or screen does, its states, variants, and any accessibility intent. Token values and layout will be left blank for a designer to fill in."

Then ask: "Is that what you're trying to do, or something different?"

---

## Step 4: Argue if intent doesn't match source

If the user confirms something that does not match what the source can produce, push back clearly. One push-back is enough. If the user insists after the explanation, proceed with their stated intent.

Examples:
- User pastes a component frame link but says they want tokens: "That link is a component, not a styles/variables frame. You won't get tokens from it — you'd get a library element and spec. Did you mean to paste your tokens frame link instead?"
- User names a prototype folder but says they want a component spec: "That's a local prototype folder, not a Figma frame. I can extract interaction specs from it, but not a component spec. For a component spec, paste a Figma link to the component frame instead."
- User pastes a screen frame but says they want a library element: "That link points to a screen, not a component. I can extract a screen spec from it, but not a library element. Paste a link to the specific component frame you want extracted."

---

## Step 5: Route

Once source and intent are confirmed, read and follow the instructions in the appropriate sub-file:

- **Reusable component (library element + spec):** read `.claude/skills/extract/library.md` and follow all steps (Mode C)
- **Tokens/styles extraction:** read `.claude/skills/extract/library.md` and follow all steps (Mode A or B)
- **Spec-only (screens, templates, flows, or spec-only components):** read `.claude/skills/extract/specs.md` and follow all steps
- **Interaction extraction:** read `.claude/skills/extract/interaction.md` and follow all steps
- **Non-Figma extraction:** read `.claude/skills/extract/non-figma.md` and follow all steps
- **Full pass:** run `library.md` (tokens, if a tokens frame exists or was identified) → `library.md` Mode C for each component frame found → `interaction.md` (all prototypes in `/02-design/prototypes/`) in sequence

---

## Step 6: Complete

Update the memory entry to: "Skill /extract completed [today's date]."

# Extract: Interaction

Instructions for extracting interaction specs from prototypes. Called by `/extract` after source identification. Updates linked spec files in `/02-design/specs`. Also run as part of the full pass via `/handover`.

The prototype folder name or path has already been provided (or this is a full pass scanning all prototypes). Do not ask for it again.

---

## Step 1: Discover prototypes

**Single prototype mode** (user named a specific folder): locate that folder under `/02-design/prototypes/`. If not found, tell the user and ask them to confirm the folder name.

**Full pass mode** (called from `/handover`): scan `/02-design/prototypes/` recursively for all folders containing `index.html`.

For each prototype:
1. Read `intent.md` to get `spec`, `stack`, and `stage` from the frontmatter
2. If `intent.md` is missing or frontmatter is incomplete, flag it: "Prototype at [path] has no intent.md or is missing required frontmatter. Skipping."

---

## Step 2: Extract token candidates from styles.css

For each prototype, read `assets/styles.css` (or any CSS file in `assets/`). Compare all CSS custom property definitions against `02-design/library/common.css`.

Any custom properties defined in `styles.css` that do not exist in `02-design/library/common.css` are candidates. Collect them.

If candidates are found, present them to the user:

> "Found [n] potential token candidates in [prototype name]:"
>
> - `--motion-easing-standard: cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)`: looks like a motion easing token
> - `--motion-duration-short: 200ms`: looks like a motion duration token
>
> Add these to `02-design/library/common.css`? (Confirm each individually or say "all" / "none")

For each confirmed candidate:
1. Add the CSS custom property to the `:root {}` block in `02-design/library/common.css`
2. Add a row to `02-design/library/tokens.md` under the appropriate section (create a Motion section if none exists)
3. Replace the definition in `assets/styles.css` with a reference: `var(--token-name)`

Never write to `02-design/library/common.css` without explicit user confirmation.

---

## Step 3: Extract interaction specs

For each prototype, read `intent.md` body and `assets/styles.css`. Extract:

- All interactions documented in `intent.md` (trigger, response, transition, haptic, duration, easing)
- All CSS transitions and animations from `styles.css`
- All JS event listeners if present (from `index.html`)

Cross-reference: flag any interaction in `styles.css` or `index.html` that is not documented in `intent.md`. Ask: "This interaction in [prototype] is not documented in intent.md. Add it?"

---

## Step 4: Update linked spec

For each prototype, open the spec file referenced in `intent.md` frontmatter (path relative to `/02-design/specs`).

- If a "Prototype" line exists in the spec, update it with the prototype path and a note of what it demonstrates
- If an "Interactions" section exists, append or update it with the extracted interaction data
- If the spec does not exist, determine the correct subfolder from the prototype's `stage` frontmatter:
  - `stage: template` → create using the template spec format from `.claude/skills/extract/specs.md` and save to `02-design/specs/templates/[name].md`
  - `stage: flow` → create using the annotation template and save to `02-design/specs/flows/[name].md`
  - All other stages (interaction, tokens, animation) → create using the annotation template from `/05-handover/platform/[stack]/annotation-template.md` and save to `02-design/specs/screens/[name].md`
- Never overwrite the Platform layer section

---

## Step 5: Prototype screenshot reminder

After completing extraction, remind the user:

> "Interaction specs extracted. One thing to do manually: take a screenshot of the prototype in the browser (or a device) and save it here:"
> `02-design/prototypes/[type]/[slug]/assets/YYYY-MM-DD-screenshot.png`
> "Use today's date in the filename. This creates a point-in-time visual record of what the prototype looked like when the spec was extracted."

---

## Step 6: Update changelogs and commit

Prepend changelog entries to each updated spec file. Commit: "Extract interaction specs: [list of prototype names]".
