These inform the grill and the scaffold. --- ## Phase 2: Grill Write a memory entry: "Skill /start-prototype started [today's date], incomplete." Open with a one-line scan summary before the questions. For example: > "Library: [no tokens / partial tokens / X colour + Y spacing tokens]. [N] components. Build: [React CDN / Vanilla] (project default). [N] existing prototypes. Token source in use: [library tokens / external / self-contained / Tailwind CDN / greyscale / mixed]." Then ask the questions in order, one per message. Wait for each answer before asking the next. --- **Question 1: Fidelity.** "What fidelity is this prototype? Wireframe (layout and structure only, greyscale), mid-fidelity (real layout and content, some token colours), or high-fidelity (full library tokens, real content, production-quality visuals)?" This determines the scaffold comment and the note in `intent.md`. --- **Question 2: Continuation or new?** Show the list of existing prototypes with their one-line intent summaries: > "Existing prototypes:" > 1. `interactions/card-expand`: demonstrates the card expanding on tap to reveal detail content > 2. `flows/onboarding-flow`: shows the four-step onboarding sequence with progress indicator > [etc.] > > "Is this prototype a continuation of one of these, or is it new?" If yes (continuation): - Ask which one: "Which prototype is this continuing from?" - Silently read the selected prototype's `intent.md` and `assets/styles.css` - Pre-fill Q3 and remaining questions with context from that prototype (name, spec, components, token candidates already in use) - Present each pre-filled answer as a default: "[Answer carried from [slug]]. Change this?" Also offer to open the selected prototype in the browser: "Want me to open [slug] in the browser first so you can see it?" If yes: run `open 02-design/prototypes/[type]/[slug]/index.html` If no (new): continue with Q3 blank. --- **Question 3: What are you prototyping?** Only ask if new. If continuation, present pre-filled name from the selected prototype as a default to confirm or change. "What are you prototyping? One sentence: name and brief description." --- **Question 4: What can Figma NOT show here?** "What does this prototype need to communicate that Figma can't? For example: state transitions, gesture responses, multi-step flows, timing-dependent animations, conditional logic, form validation feedback, responsive layout behaviour, structural regions reflowing across viewport sizes, navigation patterns changing between breakpoints." This is the intent statement. It goes into `intent.md` and justifies why this prototype exists. --- **Question 5: Prototype type.** "What type of prototype is this? - `interactions`: component state changes, hover/tap/press behaviours, micro-interactions - `flows`: navigation sequences, user journeys, screen-to-screen transitions - `tokens`: visual reference for colours, typography, spacing, motion values - `animations`: standalone animation or motion demos - `templates`: page-level HTML shell demonstrating structural regions, component placement, and responsive layout behaviour. Contains real or placeholder components. Required for any template or page spec. Note: the folder type is `templates` (plural) but the value written to the `stage` field in `intent.md` is `template` (singular). The scaffold handles this automatically." --- **Question 6: Folder slug.** "What's the folder slug? Kebab-case, becomes the folder name. Existing: [list]. Examples: `card-expand`, `onboarding-flow`, `colour-palette`." Show existing prototype folders so they can match naming conventions. --- **Question 7: Which spec does this feed into?** "Which spec does this prototype feed into? [show list of available spec files from scan, or 'No specs found yet.']" If no specs exist, they can enter "TBD". The field will be left as a placeholder in `intent.md`. --- **Question 8: [Conditional] Design target.** "What platform or device is this prototype designed for? iOS, Android, or web browser. This sets the device frame in the viewer and determines whether platform reference styles (HIG for iOS, Material Design for Android) are loaded alongside your tokens." Only ask this if design target mode is `multi-mobile`, `mixed`, or `unknown` (see Phase 1). If `mobile-only`: state which target was auto-detected and ask them to confirm. If `web-only`: skip this question entirely. If type is `templates`: skip this question regardless of mode. Template prototypes are always web. Set design target to `web` automatically and note it in the Phase 3 report. Valid values: `ios`, `android`, `web`, `react`, `angular`, `lwc` --- **Question 9: Token source.** "Where are your design tokens coming from? (a) Library tokens: `02-design/library/common.css`. Library is currently [populated / partial / empty]. Impact: prototype depends on this repo. Token changes in the library immediately affect all prototypes using it. (b) External token set: a different CSS file or URL. Impact: prototype depends on that source. Confirm it is stable and accessible before sharing. (c) Self-contained: all values defined inside `assets/styles.css`. Fully portable, no external dependency. Impact: tokens are isolated and will not be promoted to the library unless you mark and extract them manually. (d) Tailwind CDN: utility classes, no token variables. Impact: temporary, must be replaced before handover. (e) Greyscale / wireframe: neutral values only. Impact: layout exploration only, not suitable for visual review." If (a): follow up immediately: "Which tokens from the library do you plan to reference? [show scanned token list]" If (a) and library is empty: "No tokens are in the library yet. You can still choose library mode and define values in `assets/styles.css` marked `/* token candidate */`. Promote them via `/extract` later." If (b): ask for the path or URL to the external CSS file before continuing. Record the confirmed choice as the token source. Used in the scaffold and `intent.md`. --- **Question 10: Components.** "The library has [N] extracted components: [list names]. Are any of these relevant to this prototype?" If no components in library: "No components have been extracted to the library yet. Build the prototype first, then run `/extract` to add them." --- **Question 11: [Conditional] Baseline reference.** Only ask this if `01-context/project-context.md` contains baseline context or `01-context/ref-local/baseline/` has files. If so: "I found baseline context: [one-line summary from project-context]. Should this prototype reference or compare against the current state, or is it a net-new design?" If no baseline exists: skip this question. --- ## Phase 3: Report and scaffold ### Report After receiving answers, present a one-screen summary before scaffolding: ``` Prototype: [name/slug] Type: [type] Stack: [stack] Fidelity: [wireframe / mid-fi / hi-fi] Token source: [library / external: [source] / self-contained / Tailwind CDN (temporary) / greyscale] Stage: [interaction | flow | tokens | animation | template] Spec: [spec path or TBD] Baseline: [yes, referencing [source] / no] Assets available Tokens: [populated / partial / empty, and brief note] Components: [list relevant ones, or none] Gaps [List any: empty library, missing spec, platform styles not found, CDN in use, etc.] Platform guardrail [If mobile: "05-handover/platform/[stack]/README.md exists. Review before building."] [If mobile + _platform CSS exists: "02-design/prototypes/_platform/[stack].css will be linked."] [If mobile + _platform CSS missing: "WARNING: 02-design/prototypes/_platform/[stack].css not found. Run /setup-local or check the repo."] Scaffold 02-design/prototypes/[type]/[slug]/index.html 02-design/prototypes/[type]/[slug]/assets/styles.css 02-design/prototypes/[type]/[slug]/intent.md ``` Ask: "Scaffold this prototype?" --- ### Scaffold On confirmation, create the following files. #### `02-design/prototypes/[type]/[slug]/index.html` **If type is `templates`:** Scaffold a semantic page shell directly using the structure below. Do not use the standard `react-cdn.html` or `vanilla.html` templates. They are component sandboxes, not page frames. ```html [Template Name]: Template Demo
[ Header region placeholder ]
[ Main content region placeholder ]
[ Footer region placeholder ]
``` Add any additional named regions (announcement bar, sidebar, etc.) between the standard regions as needed. Each region gets a `.region-[name]` class and a `data-region` attribute matching the spec's region name. Apply the same conditional CSS link logic as below. **For all other types:** Read `.claude/skills/start-prototype/templates/react-cdn.html` or `templates/vanilla.html` (based on `prototypeStack` from config). Fill in all `[bracketed]` placeholders from the grill answers. Apply conditional include lines: - Include `common.css` link only if token source is library (a). - Include the external CSS link only if token source is external (b). Use the confirmed path or URL. - Omit any token CSS link if token source is self-contained (c), Tailwind (d), or greyscale (e). - Include the `_platform` stylesheet only if design target is `ios` or `android`. - Include the Tailwind CDN script only if the designer confirmed Tailwind (d). - React CDN scripts are always included when `prototypeStack` is `react-cdn`. Path notes (always correct, do not change): - `../../../library/common.css`: 3 levels up from `02-design/prototypes/[type]/[slug]/`. - `../../_platform/[target].css`: 2 levels up from the prototype folder. #### `02-design/prototypes/[type]/[slug]/assets/styles.css` Read `.claude/skills/start-prototype/templates/styles.css`. Fill in all `[bracketed]` placeholders from the grill answers. #### `02-design/prototypes/[type]/[slug]/intent.md` Read `.claude/skills/start-prototype/templates/intent.md`. Fill in all `[bracketed]` placeholders from the grill answers. --- ### After scaffolding Tell the designer: 1. Open `02-design/prototypes/[type]/[slug]/index.html` in a browser. It will render immediately. 2. [If react-cdn]: Build your UI as React components inside the `` in the ``. Update the memory entry to: "Skill /start-prototype completed [today's date], slug: [slug]."

2. If successful: read the content, write a summary file to `01-context/summaries/[domain-slug].md`, update status to `absorbed` in `links.md`, add to manifest.
3. If blocked by authentication: explain why ("This Confluence page requires a login. Options: (a) log in via browser, export as PDF, drop into `01-context/ref-local/`; (b) set up a Confluence MCP connection; (c) skip for now."). Update status to `auth-needed` in `links.md`.
4. If blocked by missing MCP: explain which MCP is needed and how to set it up. Update status to `mcp-needed` in `links.md`.
5. If the URL no longer exists: ask the user if this ref should be marked as `removed`.

---

## Step 5: Extract decisions

Scan all newly absorbed summary files and workshop session context blocks for design decisions, confirmed constraints, and agreed directions (explicit statements like "the client confirmed", "we decided", "it was agreed", "constraint: ...").

For each found, append a dated entry to `01-context/decisions.md`:

```markdown
**[YYYY-MM-DD]** [Decision statement in one sentence.]
Source: [summary filename or workshop session filename]
```

Do not duplicate decisions already in `decisions.md`. If a decision was already captured, skip it.

---

## Step 5.5: Dedup decisions

After appending new decisions, scan the full `decisions.md` for entries that are semantically near-identical: same underlying fact, similar phrasing, captured within a 3-day window of each other. This catches cases where two team members captured the same decision from the same meeting in separate sessions before either committed.

For each near-identical pair found, flag before moving to Step 6:

> "These two decisions look like the same fact captured twice:
>   [date] [decision A]. Source: [file]
>   [date] [decision B]. Source: [file]
> Keep both, merge into one entry, or remove the older one?"

Wait for the user's answer and apply before continuing. If no near-duplicates are found, proceed silently.

---

## Step 6: Re-synthesise project-context.md

Rewrite `01-context/project-context.md` using the template at `.claude/skills/update-context/templates/project-context.md`. Fill the manifest block from all absorbed sources. Fill the Synthesis sections from cross-cutting facts across all summary files and workshop sessions. Omit any Synthesis section that has no content. Document-specific details stay in summary files. The synthesis must stay compact.

---

## Step 7: Report and complete

Tell the user:
- [n] new summary files written to `01-context/summaries/`
- [n] workshop sessions added to manifest
- [n] external refs checked: [n] absorbed, [n] still pending (list briefly)
- [n] decisions appended to `decisions.md`
- [n] files flagged as needing export
- `project-context.md` re-synthesised

Update the memory entry to: "Skill /update-context completed [today's date]."

# Skill: /workshop

Runs a guided thinking-through session grounded in project context. Can be used to frame a problem, explore ideas, pressure-test a direction, or work through a design decision. Goal-first, question-driven, always produces a document added to the project knowledge base. Can be run multiple times.

---

## Pre-flight: Check for incomplete sessions

Check memory for any incomplete `/workshop` session. If found, surface it first:
> "[date]: A /workshop session was not completed. Continue where you left off?"
Wait for response before proceeding.

---

## Pre-flight: Path resolution

Read `.claude/skills/_shared/portability.md` and resolve paths before scanning.

Required: `contextDiscovery`
Optional: `contextProject`, `contextDecisions`, `contextSummaries`, `specs`, `library`, `prototypes`, `requirements`

---

## Phase 1: Silent context scan

Do all of this silently before showing anything to the user.

1. Read `project.config.js` for project name, client, stacks, and description.
2. Read `01-context/project-context.md` if it exists. Note existing problem statements, personas, constraints, business rules, and decisions.
3. Read `01-context/decisions.md` and any relevant files in `01-context/summaries/`.
4. Check `01-context/ref-local/baseline/` for current-state references.
5. List existing files in `01-context/discovery/`. Note dates and topics.
6. Check for specs in `02-design/specs/`, tokens in `02-design/library/tokens.md`, prototypes in `02-design/prototypes/`, requirements in `03-requirements/`.
7. Check memory for any unresolved external refs.

Assess overall context richness:
- **Rich**: project-context.md populated, multiple summaries, specs or prototypes present
- **Partial**: some context exists but gaps are visible
- **Thin**: minimal context, mostly placeholders
- **Empty**: no context files found

---

## Phase 2: Session start

Write a memory entry: "Skill /workshop started [today's date], incomplete."

Show the context snapshot and ask for the session goal in one message:

> "Context: [project/client]. [One line describing what's available: X specs, Y prototypes, Z summaries, N prior sessions.] [If thin or empty: Limited context found. Questions will be broader. Everything you share in this session will be added to the project knowledge base.]
>
> What do you want to walk away with at the end of this session? A direction, a decision, a problem framing, a rough solution, something else?
>
> Who is in this session? (Names or initials. Optional, used to document the session.)"

Record the stated goal. It anchors the question sequence and appears at the top of the output document.

---

## Phase 3: Adaptive grill

Ask questions one at a time. Wait for each answer before asking the next.

Do not follow a fixed sequence. Select and sequence questions from the bank below based on:
- The stated goal
- What is already known from context (present as pre-filled defaults, do not re-ask)
- What emerges in the conversation (follow threads, ask natural follow-ups)
- What is missing but relevant to the goal

Where context already contains a relevant fact, present it as a pre-filled default:
> "I have this from context: '[fact]'. Is this still accurate, or has it changed?"

### Question bank

Draw from these areas as relevant. Not all areas need to be covered in every session.

**Problem definition**
- What problem are we solving, or what opportunity are we exploring?
- What has triggered this session? What changed, or what is unclear?

**Users**
- Who are the users? Roles, not full personas.
- What do users need to do or feel that they currently cannot?
- Who are the primary users? Who are secondary or edge cases?

**Current state**
- Is there an existing experience this builds on, replaces, or competes with?
- What works in the current state? What is broken or missing?

**Directions and ideas**
- What directions or ideas are on the table, even rough ones?
- Which direction feels strongest right now, and why?
- What would make one direction clearly better than another?

**Constraints**
- What are the hard constraints? Platform, accessibility level, existing systems, time or budget.
- What is non-negotiable?

**Usability and accessibility**
- What usability considerations are specific to this problem or user group?
- What accessibility requirements apply: WCAG level, assistive tech, specific user needs?

**Business rules and logic**
- What rules, conditions, or logic will affect the design? Pricing tiers, permissions, workflows, validation.
- What does a prototype or implementation need to get right?

**Testing and validation**
- How would you know if a proposed direction is working?
- What assumptions need to be validated before committing to a direction?
- What is the lightest way to test this?

**Implementation**
- Are there technical or platform-specific constraints that affect the design?
- What does the dev team or target platform require?

**Known vs assumed**
- What has been validated through research, data, or stakeholder decisions?
- What is being assumed? Assumptions are design risks.

**Open questions**
- What still needs to be answered before moving forward with confidence?
- Who owns each open question?

---

## Phase 4: Wrap-up proposal

When the session goal appears to have been reached, or when the conversation has covered the relevant ground, propose wrapping up:

> "I think we have enough to write a synthesis. Here's what I'd capture:
> [bullet list: goal, key decisions or directions, main constraints, assumptions, open questions]
>
> Ready to wrap up, or are we not done yet?"

If the user is ready: proceed to Phase 5.

> "The output will cover: [goal], [key points from the session]. Anything to add, remove, or change before I write it?"

Wait for confirmation or adjustments. Then proceed to Phase 6.

# Component contract

The contract is the single source of truth for the component API. Every component
that exists (its name, tier, attributes, slots, composition, and accessibility
requirements) is recorded here. If it is not in the contract, it does not exist.

---

## What is in this folder

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `[prefix]-contract.js` | The contract: an array of component definitions. Generated and maintained by `/extract`. |
| `validate.mjs` | Checks the atomic model rules against the contract. Run before any handover. |

---

## How to read a contract entry

```js
{
  name:      "Button",          // PascalCase component name
  prefix:    "ds",              // tag namespace (from project.config.js)
  element:   "ds-button",       // the custom element tag
  atomic:    "atom",            // atom | molecule | organism
  composes:  [],                // elements this component renders in its own template
  attributes: [
    { name: "variant", type: "enum",    values: ["primary","secondary","ghost"], default: "primary" },
    { name: "size",    type: "enum",    values: ["sm","md","lg"],                default: "md" },
    { name: "disabled",type: "boolean",                                          default: false },
  ],
  slots: [
    { name: "default", description: "Button label text" },
  ],
  a11y:      "role=button, aria-disabled when disabled, keyboard: Enter and Space activate",
  status:    "final",           // draft | in-review | final
  extracted: "2026-07-07",
}
```

**`atomic`**: the component's tier, determined by what it renders in its own template:
- `atom`: renders no other component. `composes: []`.
- `molecule`: renders only atoms.
- `organism`: renders at least one molecule.

`template` and `page` are not valid contract tiers. They are layout-layer deliverables, not Custom Elements. See atomic model Rule F in `.claude/skills/_shared/atomic-model.md`.

**`composes`**: what the component's own template renders. Slotted children are not listed here (see atomic model Rule B). This determines the tier and build order: build atoms first, then molecules, then organisms.

**`attributes`**: the component's public API. These map directly to `observedAttributes` in the Custom Element. Types:
- `enum`: a fixed set of values. Use the `default` if none is passed or the value is unrecognised.
- `boolean`: present = true, absent = false.
- `string`: freeform content.

**`slots`**: named `"default"` is the element's child content. Named slots use `slot="[name]"` on a child element.

---

## How to implement a component

1. Read the contract entry for your component.
2. Build one Custom Element per entry. The `element` value is the tag to register.
3. `composes` → your imports. Build those components first.
4. `attributes` → your `observedAttributes` array and prop defaults.
5. `slots` → your shadow DOM slot elements.
6. `a11y` → bake in. Assert in tests.
7. All styles reference CSS custom properties from `02-design/library/common.css`.
   No hardcoded values.

## Definition of done (per component)

- One Custom Element matching the contract API
- All `observedAttributes` match the contract `attributes` list
- All slots match the contract `slots` list
- `composes` matches what the template actually renders
- No props or imports beyond the contract entry
- Light and dark themes verified
- `node 02-design/library/contract/validate.mjs` passes with no violations

---

## Adding a new component

If a design needs a component not in the contract, **stop and flag it** as a proposed
addition. Do not invent a component, attribute, or token outside the contract. Raising
it means agreeing on the API, classifying the tier, extracting it via `/extract`, and
adding the entry here.

---

## Running the validator

```sh
node 02-design/library/contract/validate.mjs
```

Checks contract integrity and scans all `demo.html` files for unknown element tags.
Exit 0 = clean. Exit 1 = violations listed.

content.text:
# `.claude/skills/` — ADW Workflow Engine: Research Report

All paths below are relative to the repo root `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/Zimmermann-Handover/`. Every `SKILL.md` under `.claude/skills/` (14 skills) plus all companion reference files were read in full, and cross-checked against actual repo state (read-only).

---

## Per-skill summary (by lifecycle stage)

### Setup
| Skill | Trigger / Input / Output |
|---|---|
| **`/initiate-design-project`** (`.claude/skills/initiate-design-project/SKILL.md`) | Project lead, once, on the vanilla template. Checks `CLAUDE.md` frontmatter for `project.lock` (redirects to `/setup-local` if locked); asks ~13 project-identity questions (name, client, stacks, component prefix, WCAG, prototype stack, security level, remote repo URL, etc.); writes `project.config.js`, `02-design/viewer/viewer.config.js`, `vercel.json`, the `CLAUDE.md` lock frontmatter, rewrites `README.md`, prunes `05-handover/platform/{ios,android,web}/` to the confirmed stacks, optionally chains into `/deploy-viewer`, then `git init`/push. |
| **`/setup-local`** (`.claude/skills/setup-local/SKILL.md`) | Each team member, once, after cloning. Asks name/role/optional Figma PAT, writes gitignored `CLAUDE.local.md`, scaffolds `01-context/*` if missing, and installs `post-commit`/`pre-push` from `.claude/git-hooks/` into `.git/hooks/`. |
| **`/setup`** (`.claude/skills/setup/SKILL.md`) | Anyone, once, on a non-standard/non-ADW folder layout. Scans the repo, proposes a mapping for each of the ~18 path keys, writes confirmed overrides to `project.config.js`'s `paths` key. |
| **`/setup-ai`** (`.claude/skills/setup-ai/SKILL.md`) | Anyone, per non-Claude tool. Reads `AGENTS.md` + `project.config.js`, regenerates a tool-specific context file (`.cursor/rules/project.mdc`, `.windsurfrules`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.clinerules/project.md`, `.kiro/steering/project.md`, or a custom path). |

### Context building
| Skill | Trigger / Input / Output |
|---|---|
| **`/workshop`** (`.claude/skills/workshop/SKILL.md`) | Designer/BA/PM, ad hoc. Silently scans existing context, runs an adaptive goal-driven Q&A grill, writes a synthesis to `01-context/discovery/YYYY-MM-DD-[topic].md`; can self-chain into `/update-context` (Steps 3, 5, 6 only) to absorb itself immediately. |
| **`/update-context`** (`.claude/skills/update-context/SKILL.md`) | Anyone, after adding refs or a workshop. Traverses `01-context/ref-local/` (MarkItDown conversion) and `01-context/ref-external/links.md`, writes per-source summaries to `01-context/summaries/`, extracts dated decisions into `01-context/decisions.md`, re-synthesises `01-context/project-context.md`. Honours `securityLevel`; has an explicit prompt-injection guard on all fetched/read content. |

### Design & extraction
| Skill | Trigger / Input / Output |
|---|---|
| **`/extract`** (`.claude/skills/extract/SKILL.md` + 4 sub-files) | Designer, the single entry point for all extraction. See detailed breakdown below. |

### Prototyping
| Skill | Trigger / Input / Output |
|---|---|
| **`/start-prototype`** (`.claude/skills/start-prototype/SKILL.md`) | Designer. Silently scans config/tokens/elements/specs/existing prototypes, runs an 11-question adaptive grill, scaffolds `02-design/prototypes/[type]/[slug]/{index.html, assets/styles.css, intent.md}` from `start-prototype/templates/`. |
| **`/add-to-viewer`** (`.claude/skills/add-to-viewer/SKILL.md`) | Designer, once a prototype is ready. Pulls latest (shared-file safety), discovers unregistered `index.html` prototypes, proposes a `variants` entry per prototype from `intent.md` frontmatter (confirm/edit/skip), writes `02-design/viewer/viewer.config.js`, rewrites `02-design/prototypes/INDEX.md`, back-fills `intent.md` viewer fields. |

### Feedback
| Skill | Trigger / Input / Output |
|---|---|
| **`/capture-feedback`** (`.claude/skills/capture-feedback/SKILL.md`) | Designer/PM. Needs a Figma PAT (`CLAUDE.local.md`) + file URL; calls the Figma REST API directly (comments + node-name resolution), groups by frame, writes `04-feedback/YYYY-MM-DD-figma-comments.md`. |

### Requirements
| Skill | Trigger / Input / Output |
|---|---|
| **`/requirements-scan`** (`.claude/skills/requirements-scan/SKILL.md`) | BA/PM, independent of design track. Loads `project-context.md`/`decisions.md`, reads specs under `02-design/specs/{components,screens,flows}` (templates excluded), assesses maturity (early/mid/late) to set fidelity, writes epics/features/GWT-format stories (keyed to spec Node IDs for stable re-runs) to `03-requirements/`. |

### Handover
| Skill | Trigger / Input / Output |
|---|---|
| **`/handover`** (`.claude/skills/handover/SKILL.md` + `index-generator.md` + `bmad-export.md`) | Designer, sprint end/milestone, repeatable. Runs `extract/library.md` → `extract/specs.md` → `extract/interaction.md` (full pass) in sequence, then `index-generator.md` rewrites `05-handover/index.md` (including the `Build Status` field CLAUDE.md itself reads at session start), then optionally `bmad-export.md` writes `05-handover/bmad/*`, then a summary commit/push. |

### Deployment
| Skill | Trigger / Input / Output |
|---|---|
| **`/deploy-viewer`** (`.claude/skills/deploy-viewer/SKILL.md`) | Project lead, once. Writes/verifies `vercel.json`'s root rewrite, walks the user through browser-based Vercel project linking, records the URL in `project.config.js` (`viewer.deployUrl`). |
| **`/deploy-catalog`** (`.claude/skills/deploy-catalog/SKILL.md`) | Project lead, after `/extract` has produced a contract. Adds `/catalog` rewrites to `vercel.json` (extends the `/deploy-viewer` Vercel project), commits/pushes, derives `[viewer.deployUrl]/catalog`, records it in `project.config.js` (`catalog.deployUrl`), links it into `05-handover/index.md`. |

---

## `_shared/` rules

- **`atomic-model.md`** — The single, machine-checkable rule for classifying a component as atom / molecule / organism / template / page, based strictly on what a component's *own template renders* (`composes: [...]`), never on what's slotted in. Six lettered rules: **A** icons are attribute values, not composed Icon components; **B** slotted content never raises tier; **C** templates are structure-only (no real content — real content makes it a Page); **D** a page is always an instance of exactly one template; **E** layout sections/blocks aren't components; **F** templates and pages are never Custom Elements or contract entries (spec-layer only). Plus 3 ordered edge tests and a Figma-frame-reading procedure (structural regions → semantic-HTML mapping table → stop on ambiguous names → composition → tier-by-content-majority). **Consumed by:** `extract/library.md` explicitly (tier determination); referenced by `authoring.md` and the generated `library/contract/README.md`.
- **`authoring.md`** — The Custom Element authoring contract: component (`<[prefix]-[name]>`, tag+attributes=API) vs. layout (plain semantic HTML) distinction; kebab-case/boolean/enum/string attribute rules; default vs. named slot rules; token-only styling (no hardcoded colour/spacing/font, dark/light via the same semantic tokens); 5 hard "don'ts"; a pre-done checklist (`validate.mjs` passes, both themes verified, `observedAttributes`/slots/`composes` match the contract). **Consumed by:** `extract/library.md` explicitly, during component write-up.
- **`portability.md`** — The path-resolution pre-flight almost every skill runs first. Defines the ADW default path table (`contextRoot`, `specs`, `library`, `prototypes`, `viewer`, `requirements`, `feedback`, `handover`, etc.), how `project.config.js`'s `paths` key overrides it, and the required/optional-path-missing flow (offer to create / redirect for session only / continue in limited mode; optional paths are noted silently unless they change output). **Consumed by:** `add-to-viewer`, `capture-feedback`, `deploy-viewer`, `extract`, `handover`, `requirements-scan`, `setup-ai`, `start-prototype`, `update-context`, `workshop` — i.e. everything except `setup`, `setup-local`, `initiate-design-project`, and (see Anomalies) `deploy-catalog`.

---

## Interconnections map

- **`/initiate-design-project`** → `project.config.js`, `viewer.config.js`, `vercel.json`, `CLAUDE.md` lock → read by literally every other skill; can chain straight into `/deploy-viewer`.
- **`/setup`** → `project.config.js` `paths` overrides → read by every skill's `portability.md` pre-flight.
- **`/workshop`** → `01-context/discovery/*.md` → absorbed by `/update-context`; scanned directly by `/start-prototype` and informs `/requirements-scan` via `project-context.md`/`decisions.md`.
- **`/update-context`** → `project-context.md`, `decisions.md`, `summaries/*` → read by `/start-prototype` (Phase 1), `/requirements-scan` (Step 0), `/workshop` (Phase 1). Notably *not* read by `/extract`'s actual sub-files (see Anomalies).
- **`/extract` → `library.md`** → `library/tokens.md`, `common.css`, `library/elements/*`, `library/contract/[prefix]-contract.js`, co-produced `specs/components/*.md` → contract is read by `/deploy-catalog`, `handover/index-generator.md`, and `contract/validate.mjs`; tokens/CSS read by `/start-prototype`.
- **`/extract` → `specs.md`** → `specs/{screens,flows,templates}/*.md` → primary input to `/requirements-scan` and `handover/index-generator.md`; can directly invoke `/start-prototype` for template prototypes.
- **`/extract` → `interaction.md`** → updates spec files linked via prototype `intent.md`; promotes prototype-local CSS custom properties into the library (token candidates).
- **`/start-prototype`** → `prototypes/[type]/[slug]/intent.md` → primary input to `/add-to-viewer` and to `/extract`'s `specs.md` (Path B) / `interaction.md`.
- **`/add-to-viewer`** → `viewer.config.js` `variants[]`, `prototypes/INDEX.md` → read by the deployed viewer shell and redeployed automatically by `/deploy-viewer`'s push-triggers.
- **`/requirements-scan`** → `03-requirements/*` → counted into `handover/index-generator.md`'s Requirements section.
- **`/handover`** orchestrates all three `/extract` sub-files, then `index-generator.md` (reads contract, specs, prototypes, requirements counts, context files → writes `05-handover/index.md`), then optionally `bmad-export.md` (reads tokens/CSS/specs/prototypes/index.md → writes `05-handover/bmad/*`).
- **`/deploy-viewer`** → `viewer.deployUrl` gates `/deploy-catalog`'s Vercel-project detection.
- **`/deploy-catalog`** depends on `/extract` (populated contract) and `/deploy-viewer` (Vercel project); writes back into `05-handover/index.md`.
- **`/capture-feedback`** → `04-feedback/*.md` is a dead end — nothing else in the skill set reads it (see Anomalies).

---

## `/extract` detail — the four modes (confirmed)

Per `01-context/decisions.md` (2026-07-07 entry, "ADW web component enhancement + Zimmermann project setup"), the design intent explicitly lists "Four extraction modes," and `extract/library.md`'s actual `Mode A–D` implementation matches:

| Decision-log label | `library.md` mode | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Full library extraction | **Mode A: First extraction** | `tokens.md` still has blank rows. Schema-setting run: discovers which token categories are present, proposes a tailored schema, waits for confirmation, then writes `tokens.md` + `common.css` from scratch (Schema version 1). |
| 2. Re-extraction (library) | **Mode B: Re-extraction (full token pass)** | `tokens.md` already has real values — the existing schema is source of truth. Diffs current Figma values against it: updates changed values, adds new tokens in existing sections, flags (never silently deletes) removed ones, and asks before adding a wholly new category. |
| 3. Re-extraction (single component) | **Mode C: Single component extraction** | Triggered by one Figma component-frame URL. Skips token steps (1 and 7) entirely and goes straight to component extraction (Step 2) — the shared token schema and contract are otherwise untouched. Note: despite the decision-log name, this mode covers both a brand-new component's *first* extraction and a *re*-extraction of an existing one — the routing logic in `extract/SKILL.md` sends any single confirmed component frame here regardless of whether it's new. |
| 4. Regenerate from contract | **Mode D: Regenerate from contract** | No Figma call at all. Reads the existing contract entry + `common.css`, rewrites `[prefix]-name].js`/`demo.html` from that data, then runs `validate.mjs`. |

Each successful component extraction always co-produces a spec (`extract/library.md` Step 3b: "the spec and the library element are co-produced — they are not optional relative to each other"), and every mode ends by running `node 02-design/library/contract/validate.mjs` and refusing to mark the pass complete while violations are open.

---

## Anomalies

1. **`05-handover/index.md` is unfilled template content with dead links.** The checked-in file still has raw bracket placeholders (`[Project Name]`, `[Client]`, etc.) and a section structure (merged "Design deliverables" table, "Platform guardrails") that doesn't match what `handover/index-generator.md` actually generates (separate Tokens / Components-by-tier / Contract / Screens / Flows / Templates / Prototypes / BMAD sections). Concretely, it unconditionally links `platform/ios/README.md`, `platform/ios/annotation-template.md`, `platform/android/README.md`, `platform/android/annotation-template.md` — **none of which exist** (`project.config.js` has `stacks: ["web","react"]`; only `05-handover/platform/web/` exists, correctly pruned by `/initiate-design-project` Step 5). `index-generator.md`'s real template guards this ("Only list platforms that were in the confirmed stacks... Omit others"), so the first genuine `/handover` run should self-heal it — but as of now it's a dead-link trap, and directly relevant since CLAUDE.md's own session-start protocol tells dev-side agents to treat this file as the entry point.
2. **`/deploy-catalog` skips the path-portability pre-flight every sibling skill runs.** `deploy-viewer`, `extract`, `handover`, etc. all explicitly "Read `_shared/portability.md` and resolve paths" first. `deploy-catalog/SKILL.md` has no such step — it hardcodes `02-design/catalog/index.html` and `02-design/library/contract/[prefix]-contract.js`. On a project that ran `/setup` to remap `library`/`design` paths, this skill alone would check/deploy the wrong location.
3. **`_shared/atomic-model.md`/`authoring.md` are read by fewer skills than documented.** `01-context/decisions.md` states they're "read explicitly by skills that need them (`/extract`, `/deploy-catalog`, `/handover`)." A repo-wide grep confirms only `extract/library.md` actually reads them; `/handover` reaches them only transitively (by calling `library.md`), and `/deploy-catalog` never reaches them at all.
4. **`extract/SKILL.md` resolves `contextProject` as an optional path but never uses it.** None of `library.md`, `specs.md`, `interaction.md`, `non-figma.md` reference `project-context.md`/`decisions.md`, unlike `/start-prototype`, `/requirements-scan`, and `/workshop`. Confirmed business rules/constraints captured via `/update-context` currently don't inform spec or token extraction.
5. **`/capture-feedback` output is a dead end.** Grep confirms `04-feedback/` is referenced only by `capture-feedback/SKILL.md` itself and the generic path table in `portability.md` — no skill folds captured Figma comments into `/requirements-scan` or `/workshop`.
6. **No skill maintains `AGENTS.md`.** `/setup-ai` treats it as a read-only source of truth for generating tool-specific context files, but none of the 14 skills write or update `AGENTS.md` — its sync with `CLAUDE.md` is manual/outside the skill system.
7. **`/setup` hand-duplicates `portability.md`'s path table** instead of reading it — an 18-item list maintained in two places that must be kept in lockstep manually (grep confirms `setup/SKILL.md` never references `portability.md`).
8. **`start-prototype`'s design-target-mode table has an undefined case this project actually hits.** The table's rows are "single mobile," "single web stack" (one of `web`/`react`/`angular`/`lwc`), "multiple all-mobile," "mixed mobile+web," or "empty" — but Zimmermann's real `stacks: ["web", "react"]` is *two* non-mobile values, matching none of the rows literally.
9. **Minor/cosmetic:** `/initiate-design-project` prunes unused `05-handover/platform/{ios,android}/` folders but not the parallel `02-design/prototypes/_platform/{ios,android}.css` — both still ship in this web/react-only project.
10. **Data-state gap (not a skill bug):** 6 of the 8 currently-extracted library elements (`button`, `icon`, `logo`, `nav-item`, `product-card`, `add-to-wishlist`) have no matching file in `02-design/specs/components/` (only `footer.md` and `navigation.md` exist), even though `extract/library.md` Step 3b now guarantees spec+element are co-produced — likely a pre-existing extraction batch from before that step was added, worth flagging to the design team.
